newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Southern falls on poor investment showing.
newsitem.headline: Southern falls on poor investment showing.

text.p: Shares in South African life assurer Southern Life Association Ltd fell over eight percent in brisk dealings on Thursday after year results released on Wednesday revealed a disappointing investment performance, dealers said.
Shares fell 360 cents to 41 rand, nearing a year low of 39 rand making Southern the second worst performer on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) at one stage on Thursday.
However, by 0850 GMT shares had recovered slightly to 42 rand, a drop of 260 cents after 120,500 shares had traded.
"On the face of it the results looked good, but if one looks at the underlying investment performance it was not so hot," one dealer said.
Southern said on Wednesday that its total assets amounted to 32,562 million rand on March 31 1997, down from 32,857 billion a year before.

"This lack of growth was largely attributable to a lacklustre JSE perforamnce, a 19 percent decline in the share price of our largest holding, First National Bank, and retirment fund investment withdrawals and terminations of 2,618 million rand," Southern said.
The group reported year earnings per share up at 267.0 cents from 216.0 before and a dividend of 178.0 cents from 144.0.
Dealres said that they would recommend holding shares at 40 rand.
"It is a good recovery stock, and people should top up from 40 rand," a dealer said.
